status: first pass. Source types follow the referrals engine brief (13 categories). default_points, niche weights, type boosts and the session-capped boost are judgment calls (no source measures referral share by source type), labelled as such; the seven types that match referral-tiers.json keep its specialty points. Every NUCC code below was seen in a live Illinois NPPES result and is in NUCC v26.1; NPPES search strings were checked live. Not yet used by tier scoring (next PR).

sources.what: NUCC Health Care Provider Taxonomy code set v26.1 (CSV)
NPPES NPI Registry API v2.1 (taxonomy_description + state=IL)
CMS Provider Data Catalog: Hospice - General Information
CMS Provider Data Catalog: Home Health Care Agencies
Medicare hospice bereavement counseling (42 CFR 418.64(d)(1), up to 1 year after death)

findable_via.nppes: NPI Registry search by nppes_searches; keep only primary codes in nucc_codes (lib/referrals/nppes.ts SPECIALTIES)
findable_via.cms_dataset: CMS Provider Data Catalog dataset by ZIP (cms_dataset.id)
findable_via.osm_tags: OpenStreetMap features with these tags (Overpass, rate-limited, ODbL attribution)
findable_via.public_list: A public directory or list (state bar, state licensing, school or hospital websites); added by hand or CSV
findable_via.manual: Not in any dataset; she adds them by hand

points_note: default_points is the score before niche weighting, on the same 0-35 scale as the specialty factor in referral-tiers.json. Manual sources default to 18 there; these replace that default per type. Judgment.

types.label: Family medicine
types.why_they_refer: First stop for anxiety, depression and stress, with no one in-house to send them to.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who answers fast, says when she has openings and sends a short note back when the patient allows it.
talk_track.you_offer: Your openings, fee and superbill policy on one page, and a direct line for the front desk.

types.label: Internal medicine
types.why_they_refer: Sees adults with stress, anxiety and depression alongside chronic illness.

talk_track.they_need: Somewhere reliable to send adults who need more than a quick check-in.
talk_track.you_offer: A clear list of who you see and how a patient books a first consult.

types.label: Pediatrics
types.why_they_refer: Child and teen behavior, ADHD follow-up and parent stress land on their desk.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who sees their age group and talks to parents in plain words.
talk_track.you_offer: The ages you see, whether you work with parents, and your wait time.

types.label: OB/GYN
types.why_they_refer: Screens for perinatal mood, pregnancy loss and infertility stress at routine visits.

talk_track.they_need: A perinatal-ready therapist who can see someone within a couple of weeks.
talk_track.you_offer: Your perinatal focus, video options and how quickly you can see a new parent.

types.label: Midwives
types.why_they_refer: Follow pregnancy and the months after birth closely, so they see mood changes early.

talk_track.they_need: Someone gentle and quick for parents who are struggling after birth.
talk_track.you_offer: Perinatal openings, home-friendly video sessions and a short intro sheet.

types.label: Geriatrics
types.why_they_refer: Grief, adjustment to aging and caregiver strain come up in every visit.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist comfortable with older adults and their families, with no stairs to climb or video help.
talk_track.you_offer: Your work with older adults and caregivers, and accessibility details for your office.

types.note: Geriatric codes stay inside the family medicine and internal medicine searches so existing cards keep their kind; the tier PR can split them.

types.label: Nurse practitioners and PAs
types.why_they_refer: Often the person a patient actually sees for primary care.

talk_track.they_need: A quick way to hand off a patient who needs ongoing therapy.
talk_track.you_offer: A one-page how-to-refer sheet and your current openings.

types.note: Family, women's health, pediatric and psychiatric NPs stay with their own fields.

types.label: Concierge and direct primary care
types.why_they_refer: Cash-pay patients who expect fast, personal care; a strong fit for private pay.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who matches their service level and can see people soon.
talk_track.you_offer: Private-pay fee, superbill policy and how fast you schedule a consult.

types.note: No NUCC code marks concierge practice; found from their own websites.

types.label: Urgent care and retail clinics
types.why_they_refer: See panic attacks and crisis follow-ups with nowhere to send people next.

talk_track.they_need: A short list of therapists taking new clients this month.
talk_track.you_offer: A small card or flyer with how to book and that 988 is for emergencies.

types.label: Oncology and hematology
types.why_they_refer: Distress, fear of recurrence and family strain follow a cancer diagnosis.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who understands treatment schedules and can flex around them.
talk_track.you_offer: Your serious-illness focus, video sessions on treatment days and a direct contact for the nurse navigator.

types.label: Cardiology
types.why_they_refer: Depression after a heart attack and health anxiety are common and under-treated.

talk_track.they_need: Someone to send patients whose worry is slowing their recovery.
talk_track.you_offer: Your chronic-illness focus and how to book.

types.label: Neurology
types.why_they_refer: MS, brain injury, epilepsy and dementia bring adjustment and family stress.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist used to working around fatigue and memory changes.
talk_track.you_offer: Your experience with chronic and neurological illness and caregiver sessions.

types.label: Gastroenterology
types.why_they_refer: IBS and other gut-brain conditions respond to therapy.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who takes gut-brain referrals seriously.
talk_track.you_offer: Whether you offer gut-directed or health-focused work and your openings.

types.label: Endocrinology
types.why_they_refer: Diabetes distress, thyroid changes and gender-affirming care raise mental health needs.

talk_track.they_need: Someone who understands living with a chronic condition day to day.
talk_track.you_offer: Your chronic-illness focus and affirming-care stance.

types.label: Rheumatology
types.why_they_refer: Chronic pain and flares wear on mood and coping.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who works with chronic pain and coping.
talk_track.you_offer: Your chronic pain focus and flexible video sessions.

types.label: Pain management
types.why_they_refer: Pain programs need therapy alongside procedures and medication.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who does pain-focused work and reports back on engagement when allowed.
talk_track.you_offer: Your pain-focused approach and how quickly you can start.

types.label: Sleep medicine
types.why_they_refer: CBT for insomnia is the first-line treatment and few therapists offer it.

talk_track.they_need: Someone who offers CBT for insomnia or knows who does.
talk_track.you_offer: Whether you offer CBT-I and your openings.

types.label: Fertility clinics
types.why_they_refer: IVF stress, loss and donor decisions need a therapist who knows the process.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist fluent in fertility treatment and loss.
talk_track.you_offer: Your reproductive focus and couples sessions.

types.note: Reproductive endocrinology stays inside the OB/GYN search so existing cards keep their kind; clinic names come from their websites.

types.label: Bariatric surgery programs
types.why_they_refer: Require a psych evaluation before surgery and support after.

talk_track.they_need: Clinicians who do pre-surgical evaluations or post-surgery support on time.
talk_track.you_offer: What you can and can't do (evaluations or ongoing therapy) and your turnaround.

types.note: No NUCC code for bariatric surgery (NPPES matches 'Bariatric' only to obesity medicine); programs are listed on hospital websites.

types.label: Plastic and reconstructive surgery
types.why_they_refer: Body image concerns and reconstruction after cancer come up before and after surgery.

talk_track.they_need: Someone for patients whose expectations or distress worry them.
talk_track.you_offer: Your body-image or serious-illness focus.

types.label: Transplant programs
types.why_they_refer: Require psychosocial evaluations and long-term support.

talk_track.they_need: Clinicians who understand transplant timelines and caregiver strain.
talk_track.you_offer: Your serious-illness focus and caregiver sessions.

types.note: Found on hospital websites, not NPPES.

types.label: Dermatology
types.why_they_refer: Psychodermatology: skin conditions and body image weigh on mood.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist for patients whose skin condition affects how they live.
talk_track.you_offer: Your body-image and chronic-illness focus.

types.label: Genetic counselors
types.why_they_refer: BRCA and other results bring family risk decisions and worry.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who can help someone live with a result and talk to family.
talk_track.you_offer: Your serious-illness and family focus.

types.label: Physiatry and rehab medicine
types.why_they_refer: Injury and disability bring adjustment and loss of role.

talk_track.they_need: Someone who works with adjustment after injury.
talk_track.you_offer: Your chronic-illness and trauma focus and accessible office details.

types.label: Psychiatry
types.why_they_refer: Their patients need therapy alongside medication, and few psychiatrists do it themselves.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who coordinates with releases on file and sees patients weekly.
talk_track.you_offer: Your openings, approach and how you coordinate care with consent.

types.label: Child and adolescent psychiatry
types.why_they_refer: Child and teen patients need weekly therapy and parent work.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who sees their ages and works with parents.
talk_track.you_offer: The ages you see and your parent sessions.

types.note: Inside the psychiatry search (2084P08*).

types.label: Psychiatric-mental health NPs
types.why_they_refer: The fastest-growing prescriber group, often without in-house therapy.

talk_track.they_need: A dependable therapist to pair with medication management.
talk_track.you_offer: Your openings and how you coordinate with prescribers.

types.note: Inside the psychiatry specialty (363LP0808X).

types.label: Addiction medicine
types.why_they_refer: Medication treatment works best with therapy alongside it.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist comfortable working with someone in recovery.
talk_track.you_offer: Whether you see people in recovery and how you coordinate.

types.label: Solo therapists (LCSW, LCPC, LMFT)
types.why_they_refer: Full caseloads or clients outside their niche; referrals go both ways.

talk_track.they_need: A colleague to send overflow and out-of-niche clients to.
talk_track.you_offer: Your niche, your openings, and the kinds of clients you send out in return.

types.label: Psychologists
types.why_they_refer: Testing and evaluation referrals run both directions.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist for ongoing care after an evaluation.
talk_track.you_offer: Your openings, and clients you'd send for testing.

types.note: Inside the therapists specialty (103T*).

types.label: Group practices
types.why_they_refer: Overflow and waitlists, especially for niches they don't cover.

talk_track.they_need: Somewhere to send waitlisted or out-of-niche clients.
talk_track.you_offer: Your niche and current openings, updated monthly.

types.note: Organization (NPI-2) records in the therapists search.

types.label: Niche specialists (couples, sex therapy, eating disorders, trauma, OCD)
types.why_they_refer: Cases outside their scope go to a trusted colleague.

talk_track.they_need: A colleague who covers what they don't.
talk_track.you_offer: Your niche, plus the cases you'd send to them.

types.note: Found in NPPES as therapists; the niche itself only shows on their own website.

types.label: IOP, PHP and residential programs
types.why_they_refer: Step-down after discharge needs an outpatient therapist ready to go.

talk_track.they_need: Outpatient therapists who can take a step-down client within a week of discharge.
talk_track.you_offer: Fast intake for step-downs and how you coordinate with their team.

types.label: Inpatient psychiatric discharge planners
types.why_they_refer: Need aftercare appointments before a patient leaves.

talk_track.they_need: A therapist who can book an aftercare appointment quickly.
talk_track.you_offer: A direct number and your soonest openings.

types.label: Crisis teams and 988 centers
types.why_they_refer: Stabilized callers need ongoing outpatient care.

talk_track.they_need: Outpatient therapists taking new clients.
talk_track.you_offer: Your openings and how to book; you do not provide crisis services.

types.note: Crisis services are short by design and hand people off.

types.label: University training clinics
types.why_they_refer: Clients beyond what trainees can take on.

talk_track.they_need: Licensed clinicians for complex cases.
talk_track.you_offer: Your niche and openings.

types.label: Clinical supervisors and consultation groups
types.why_they_refer: Trusted handoffs between colleagues they know.

talk_track.they_need: Colleagues they can vouch for.
talk_track.you_offer: Your niche and a short profile they can pass on.

types.label: Hospital social workers and case managers
types.why_they_refer: Discharge plans need outpatient therapy lined up.

talk_track.they_need: Therapists who answer quickly and take the patient's situation in stride.

types.label: Nurse navigators (cancer, cardiac, transplant)

niche_presets.note: Judgment calls, not measured. A type's points become default_points x category weight x type boost (1 when not listed). 1 is neutral; 1.5 is the brief's highest-weighted categories.

presets.label: Oncology / serious illness / end of life

session_capped_boost.note: Programs with a session cap (EAPs, college counseling, hospice bereavement, free short-term nonprofit counseling) hand clients off when the cap runs out. Added after niche weighting, before the 100 cap. Judgment.

hard_rules: Sensitive types (domestic violence and sexual assault agencies): never map or display a street address; contact only through their public channels.
No source type, weight or talk track may offer or reward anything of value for a referral.
Talk tracks are about practice logistics (openings, fees, how to book), never clinical advice or a client's details.
